matchups.recap: Rob got absolutely obliterated this week, losing by 19.4 points like he forgot half his roster existed on Sunday. Ben's team showed up ready to work while Rob's looked like he set his lineup Wednesday morning and then ghosted it—probably distracted thinking about how he's gonna explain this ass-kicking to the group chat. At 96.5 points, Rob's putting up offensive lineman numbers while everyone else is actually trying to win. Better luck next week, chief—you're gonna need it.

Nori got absolutely skull-fucked this week, losing by nearly 24 points to Veton like he showed up to the draft drunk and forgot he was supposed to be playing fantasy football. This wasn't even close—it was a full-on ass-whipping that made his entire roster look like a collection of waiver wire scraps that should've stayed on the wire. Maybe next time don't field what looks like a team assembled by someone who thinks "bye week strategy" means just not showing up to games.

Faton got absolutely cock-blocked by 4.6 points, which is fitting because that's probably the closest he's gotten to anything satisfying all season. He managed to scrape together 109 points and STILL couldn't close the deal against Arben, who showed up looking like he actually knows what a waiver wire is. Better luck next week, my guy—maybe try not leaving your season-winning potential on the bench like you left it in your pants.

Ilir got absolutely cock-slapped by a 26.7-point margin, which is honestly impressive considering he managed to score 77.9 points and still lose that badly—that's like showing up to a knife fight with a broken spoon. Flamur's 104.6 wasn't even his final form and it still felt like watching someone curb-stomp a toddler. Ilir's roster this week was so anemic it made a blood bank look like a juice cleanse, and next week's matchup should come with a mercy rule.

Jetmir and Peter got closer to victory than a couple of guys sharing a roster should ever get, only to choke it away by 2.8 pathetic points—basically the fantasy equivalent of blueballing each other all season. Two heads, two sets of waiver wire claims, and still couldn't outscore Rinor's mid-tier bullshit by more than a field goal's worth of fantasy points. At least when you're co-managing a team this badly, you've got someone else to blame at the bar next week.

Rilind got absolutely skull-fucked this week, losing by 23.6 points like he accidentally drafted his entire bench in the third round. Adam put up 111.5 and still probably left 30 points on his bench while Rilind's team did what it does best—choke harder than a rookie learning to swallow. That's not a matchup, that's a fucking mercy killing.

matchups.preview: Rob's sitting pretty at 2-5 like he's having a career year, but let's be real—he's just been treading water in a sea of mediocrity while Veton's down there drowning at 1-6. This week, Rob gets to feel like he's in first place for exactly seven days before reality sets back in, but hey, at least one of you basement dwellers will get to limp out of the cellar with a W. Spoiler alert: Rob's probably still going to find a way to lose this.

Faton's sitting pretty at 4-3, but let's be real—that record is held together by duct tape and prayer, and Ben's coming in desperate to stay alive at 3-4. This is the kind of matchup where Faton gets cute with his lineup, benches his best player out of sheer stubbornness, and watches Ben accidentally back into a win because his waiver pickups finally decided to show up. Faton's about to learn that being .500 doesn't mean you're safe—it means you're on the chopping block, and Ben's got nothing to lose.

Two teams with identical records about to find out which one actually deserves to be .500 and which one's just been lucky as hell. Ilir's been coasting on fumes while Nori's holding on by a thread, so whoever chokes harder this week gets the privilege of knowing they're frauds—my money's on both of you somehow managing it.

Arben's rolling in at 6-1 like he actually knows what he's doing, but let's be real—he's about to run into a Jetmir/Peter squad that's been quietly fixing all the dumb shit they were doing in weeks 1 and 2, and now they're hungry. Arben's got one loss and he's probably convinced himself he's some fantasy genius, but momentum is a cruel mistress, and this is exactly the week his "elite" roster remembers how to choke when it matters. Time for Arben to learn that 6-1 doesn't mean shit when you run into a team that's actually figured out how to execute.

Rilind's bringing a 1-6 dumpster fire to face the league's hottest team, and honestly this might be the most lopsided matchup we've seen all season—Flamur's been executing while Rilind's been out here playing like he drafted with his eyes closed. Flamur's about to add another W to the pile and send Rilind further into the basement where he clearly belongs.

Adam's sitting at 3-4 with what looks like a roster built by someone playing fantasy football for the first time, while Rinor actually knows how to manage a team and squeaked into respectability at 4-3. This week Adam's going to get absolutely dad-dicked by someone who actually understands waiver wire strategy—Rinor's about to remind him why you can't just draft a kicker in Round 6 and hope for the best.
